# Proof Dependency Graph

> **Third-party library visualization, not core Flow.** Interactive, module-level `import` graph over the `flow-verify` catalog. Generated by [`scripts/build_wiki.py`](https://github.com/flooooooooooow/flow/blob/main/scripts/build_wiki.py) on every wiki build.

## What this shows

Each node is a **module**, one `.flow` file under `lib/verify/` or `examples/verify/math/derived/`, not an individual theorem. An edge `A → B` means module `A` has an `import` line that pulls a lemma from module `B`.

| Node color | Source |
|------------|--------|
| 🔵 blue | `lib/verify/*.flow`, the 24 core modules (Peano arithmetic, order, algebra, …) |
| 🟣 purple | `examples/verify/math/derived/*.flow`, derived corpus proofs that build on core lemmas or on each other |
| ⚪ gray | External imports (e.g. a stdlib companion file referenced from a `.flow` proof) |

Click a node to see its module id and connection count, and to jump straight to its `.proof.md` page in the wiki.

## Why not every proof?

The `flow-verify` corpus has 1000+ proof files, but only `lib/verify/` and `examples/verify/math/derived/` actually use the `import` mechanism, Euclid's *Elements*, geometry, circuits, analysis, transforms, and systems examples are each self-contained, single-theorem files with zero imports. Graphing those would add hundreds of disconnected dots with no dependency information, so the builder:

1. Includes **all** of `lib/verify/` (it's small and it's the dependency anchor set).
2. Includes only the `examples/verify/math/derived/` modules that are actually part of an import edge (either they import something, or something imports them).

This keeps the graph at a couple hundred nodes, well under the ~800-node budget, with no sampling or truncation needed today. If the corpus grows a wider `import` surface later, the same builder can extend to more directories or cap by node degree (see the comment above `build_proof_graph()` in `scripts/build_wiki.py`).

## Data

The graph is served as a static `proof-graph.json` (wiki root) with the shape:

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "verify.Nat", "label": "Nat", "group": "lib", "path": "third-party/flow-verify/proofs/lib/Nat.proof.md" }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "from": "examples.math.derived.Nat-plus-assoc", "to": "verify.Nat" }
  ]
}
```

The viewer (`site/proof-graph.html`) is vanilla JS + Canvas, no charting library. It runs a small force-directed layout for a fixed number of frames, then **stops animating** once the graph settles (no continuous redraw loop, so it won't spin up the CPU or drain a phone battery). Pan by dragging, zoom with scroll/pinch, and filter modules with the search box or the legend toggles.
